title: Common Peroneal Nerve

positions.as_written: It should be tested and recorded at the first assessment of any lateral knee injury.
Examine the nerve before any lateral operation and again afterwards.
Expect the nerve to be palpable at the neck in most people.
Avoid pressure at the fibular neck in any dressing, cast or positioning, because the nerve lies on bone there with nothing over it.
Treat the nerve as the fixed point of the lateral side and the ligaments as what is arranged around it.
Identify the nerve rather than avoid its territory in any posterolateral approach.
Document dorsiflexion, eversion and first web space sensation before and after.
Consider the nerve when planning any correction that lengthens the lateral side.
Avoid long mobilisation when a short one will do, because each centimetre takes segmental supply with it.
